Based on the chest X-ray findings in the given case of a 24-year-old male with suspected Goodpasture's syndrome, which of the following options best describes the radiological pattern observed and supports the diagnosis? Consider the distribution, symmetry, and progression of findings over the imaging timeline.

A) Unilateral air space opacities predominantly in the upper lobes
B) Bilateral symmetrical air space opacities with sparing of the apices and costophrenic angles
C) Bilateral asymmetrical air space opacities with evidence of cardiomegaly
D) Diffuse bilateral air-space consolidations with apical involvement and costophrenic blunting
E) Predominantly reticulonodular pattern with significant hilar lymphadenopathy
F) Focal consolidation in the lower lobes with a pleural effusion
